located over Dry Tortugas Light, or over Fort Jefferson, moving
northwest at 10 knots.

Ecological Reserve North.

rough and confused seas, occasional lightning strikes, and
potentially blinding downpours. Get to a safe port as quickly, and as
safely as possible. When downpours reduce visibility, slow down.

properties.areaDesc: Grande Ronde Valley
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 16 at 8:04PM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
Elevated fire weather conditions persist through the overnight
hours tonight in the Grande Ronde Valley as dry air and breezy to
locally windy conditions continue. Minimum relative humidity
levels will improve up to 30-35% through the evening hours with
fair to moderate overnight recoveries expected. Sustained winds,
however, will continue to be 20-30 mph with gusts up to 35 mph
through the overnight hours. Winds will weaken as we head into
the mid to late morning hours on Saturday.

There also exist a chance of localized blowing dust associated
with the breezy winds that can bring major impacts to visibility
along roadways, including portions of interstate 84.

properties.headline: Typhoon Warning issued October 17 at 11:12AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT....Typhoon conditions, including winds of 64 knots or more
are expected.

* WHERE...Guam and Rota Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Onset of damaging winds beginning Saturday night. Onset of
destructive winds Sunday morning. Damaging winds will continue into
at least Sunday night, possibly longer if conditions warrant.

* IMPACTS...Destructive winds will produce dangerous seas that
could damage, capsize or sink vessels, along with drastically
reducing visibilities in heavy rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Typhoon Champi (29W) continues to move quickly
toward the Marianas. The exact path of 29W remains subject to
change. However, guidance supports a passage through Guam coastal
waters, with damaging winds moving in late tonight and lasting
into at least Sunday night. Champi is expected to strengthen
further today as it approaches, then move through the region as a
typhoon Sunday morning. Seas will quickly rise, with significant
sea heights reaching as high as 35 feet during closest passage of
Champi. Dangerous sea conditions may continue into Monday.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for the passage of a
typhoon Sunday morning. Secure all vessels. Conditions are expected
to be catastrophic for small craft, and extremely dangerous for any
vessels of larger size. As Tropical Storm Champi approaches, stay in
safe harbor.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 16 at 6:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has issued an air quality alert due to
increased fine particle pollution from wildfire smoke.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in the areas of San Clemente, Dana Point, San Juan
Capistrano, and Laguna Niguel. Levels of particle pollution can
vary by time and location depending on fire activity and local
weather conditions.

* WHEN...from 4 PM Friday to 10 AM Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Particles in wildfire smoke can get deep into the lungs
and cause serious health problems such as heart attacks, strokes,
asthma attacks, and difficulty breathing. Everyone can be affected,
but people with lung or heart disease, older adults, people who are
pregnant, children, and those who spend a lot of time outdoors are
at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, if you smell or see smoke:

* Remain indoors with windows and doors closed
* Avoid intense outdoor physical activity
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* If you must be outdoors, keep the time brief and wear a well-
fitting N-95 mask
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment

For the latest air quality forecasts and information, visit the
website at aqmd.gov.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Hatteras Island
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 16 at 8:46PM EDT until October 17 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip
currents, large breaking waves expected, and strong longshore
currents in the surf zone. For the High Surf Advisory, large
breaking waves of 5 to 14 feet expected in the surf zone. For
the Coastal Flood Watch, up to one foot of inundation above
ground level possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and
tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT Saturday
through Saturday evening. For the High Surf Advisory, from 2
PM Saturday to 8 AM EDT Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch,
from Saturday afternoon through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Numerous road closures and flooding of vehicles
will be possible. Vulnerable portions of NC-12 may be inundated,
especially around high tide. Dangerous swimming and surfing
conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. Dangerous
shore break can throw a swimmer or surfer head first into the
bottom causing neck and back injuries. Strong longshore
currents will create dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This has the potential to be a long
duration event bringing more significant ocean overwash impacts
to vulnerable oceanside areas through multiple high tide cycles
into next week. Minor soundside water level rises will also be
possible.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 16 at 5:42PM PDT until October 17 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
...HIGH RISK FOR RAPID FIRE GROWTH AND EXTREME FIRE BEHAVIOR WITH
ANY NEW FIRE STARTS THROUGH SATURDAY, DUE TO MODERATE TO LOCALLY
STRONG SANTA ANA WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY...

Moderate to locally strong Santa Ana winds have peaked today then
will slowly weaken tonight through Saturday. The gusty offshore
winds combined with very warm and dry conditions will maintain
Red Flag Warnings for most of Los Angeles and Ventura Counties
through Saturday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Santa Clarita Valley, Ventura County Beaches,
Ventura County Inland Coast, Lake Casitas, Ojai Valley,
Central Ventura County Valleys, Malibu Coast, Calabasas and
Agoura Hills, Western San Fernando Valley, Eastern San
Fernando Valley, Southeastern Ventura County Valleys and Los
Angeles County San Gabriel Valley.

* TIMING...Until 8 PM PDT Saturday.

* WINDS...Northeast to east 20 to 35 mph with gusts of 40 to 50
mph tonight, lowering to 15 to 30 mph with gusts 30 to 45 mph
on Saturday.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimums of 8 to 15 percent common. Poor
overnight recoveries in the foothills and wind prone areas.

* IMPACTS...If fire ignition occurs, conditions are favorable
for extreme fire behavior which would threaten life and
property.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. Use extreme caution
with anything that can spark a wildfire. Residents near wildland
interfaces should be prepared to evacuate if a wildfire breaks
out. See readyforwildfire.org and wildfirerisk.org for
information.

properties.areaDesc: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued October 17 at 10:25AM ChST until October 19 at 4:00AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large
breaking waves up to 35 feet for Guam, 20 to 25 feet for Rota,
and 15 to 20 feet for Tinian and Saipan.

* WHERE...Guam, Rota, Tinian and Saipan.

* WHEN...From 5 PM this afternoon to 4 AM ChST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low-lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will
be inundated. Shoreline erosion will occur. Breaking waves can
sweep people off their feet, and into dangerous seas. Life-
threatening swimming conditions and significant beach erosion can
be expected. Coastal inundation of 5 to 7 feet for Guam, 2 to 4
feet for Rota and 1 to 3 feet for Tinian and Saipan is possible
along with coastal flooding and beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Surf is expected to rise rapidly to dangerous
levels tonight. Coastal impacts to the western coast of Guam and
Rota are highly dependent on the final track of Champi; passage
south of Guam would be reduced impacts whereas passage over Guam
would result in larger coastal inundation.
properties.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay well away from the coast.

properties.headline: Typhoon Warning issued October 17 at 9:13AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
...TYPHOON CHAMPI MOVING WEST-NORTHWEST TOWARDS GUAM...

.NEW INFORMATION...
Champi upgraded to a typhoon.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides information and recommended actions for
people on Guam, and on Rota, Tinian and Saipan in the Northern
Marianas.

.WATCHES/WARNINGS...
A Typhoon Warning continues for Guam and Rota.
A Tropical Storm Warning in conjuction with a Typhoon Watch continue
for Tinian and Saipan.
A Coastal Flood Warning is in effect for Guam, Rota, Tinian and
Saipan.

A Flood Watch is in effect for all of Guam and the Northern
Marianas. Please listen closely for any Flash Flood Warnings that
might be in effect for your area.

Please check the latest public and marine forecasts for detailed
information about additional hazards.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 700 AM ChST, the center of Typhoon Champi (29W) was located near
latitude 12.0N and longitude 149.6E. This was about 340 miles east-
southeast of Guam. Storm motion was west-northwest, 295 degrees, at
15 mph. Storm intensity was 85 mph. The system is expected to further
intensify today, with rapid intensification likely as Champi
approaches the Marianas. This general forecast track will take
Champi just south of Guam as a category 3 typhoon.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Showers and winds will steadily increase this afternoon, and then
deteriorate significantly from tonight as newly upgraded Typhoon
Champi continues to move in from the east-southeast. Champi is
expected to go through a period of rapid intensification shortly,
strengthening further as the day goes on. Winds and rain will come
in rapidly, with winds becoming dangerous and life threatening very
soon after onset. Do not let a false sense of normalcy now dictate
your actions tomorrow; prepare NOW!
properties.instruction:
Make the final preparations to protect life and property. Rush to
completion the hardening of your home or business by closing shutters
and bracing garage doors.

If evacuating, leave as soon as possible. Guard against being stuck
out on roadways when dangerous winds and heavy rains arrive. Again,
do not stay in a metal roof or container home. Remember, pets are not
allowed in most official shelters, so check ahead with your intended
shelter.

If staying in a home, turn the refrigerator to maximum cold and keep
it closed. Turn off propane tanks and unplug small appliances. Fill
the bathtub with water in case the tap water becomes unavailable
after the storm. This is for cleaning and flushing purposes. Do not
drink it.

properties.headline: Typhoon Warning issued October 17 at 9:13AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
...TYPHOON CHAMPI MOVING WEST-NORTHWEST TOWARDS GUAM...

.NEW INFORMATION...
Champi upgraded to a typhoon.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides information and recommended actions for
people on Guam, and on Rota, Tinian and Saipan in the Northern
Marianas.

.WATCHES/WARNINGS...
A Typhoon Warning continues for Guam and Rota.
A Tropical Storm Warning in conjuction with a Typhoon Watch continue
for Tinian and Saipan.
A Coastal Flood Warning is in effect for Guam, Rota, Tinian and
Saipan.

A Flood Watch is in effect for all of Guam and the Northern
Marianas. Please listen closely for any Flash Flood Warnings that
might be in effect for your area.

Please check the latest public and marine forecasts for detailed
information about additional hazards.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 700 AM ChST, the center of Typhoon Champi (29W) was located near
latitude 12.0N and longitude 149.6E. This was about 340 miles east-
southeast of Guam. Storm motion was west-northwest, 295 degrees, at
15 mph. Storm intensity was 85 mph. The system is expected to further
intensify today, with rapid intensification likely as Champi
approaches the Marianas. This general forecast track will take
Champi just south of Guam as a category 3 typhoon.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Showers and winds will steadily increase this afternoon, and then
deteriorate significantly from tonight as newly upgraded Typhoon
Champi continues to move in from the east-southeast. Champi is
expected to go through a period of rapid intensification shortly,
strengthening further as the day goes on. Winds and rain will come
in rapidly, with winds becoming dangerous and life threatening very
soon after onset. Do not let a false sense of normalcy now dictate
your actions tomorrow; prepare NOW!
properties.instruction:
Make the final preparations to protect life and property. Rush to
completion the hardening of your home or business by closing shutters
and bracing garage doors.

If evacuating, leave as soon as possible. Guard against being stuck
out on roadways when dangerous winds and heavy rains arrive. Again,
do not stay in a metal roof or container home. Remember, pets are not
allowed in most official shelters, so check ahead with your intended
shelter.

If staying in a home, turn the refrigerator to maximum cold and keep
it closed. Turn off propane tanks and unplug small appliances. Fill
the bathtub with water in case the tap water becomes unavailable
after the storm. This is for cleaning and flushing purposes. Do not
drink it.

properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING FOR PORTIONS OF SOUTHEAST TEXAS AND CENTRAL
AND SOUTHWEST LOUISIANA FRIDAY AND SATURDAY...

.Breezy and dry conditions due to a frontal passage will combine
with very dry fuels resulting in a period of high fire danger.
Red flag conditions will develop across portions of central and
southwest Louisiana and southeast Texas Friday afternoon and
evening, before winds decrease and humidity recovers some
overnight. Red flag conditions will then be expected again across
all of central and southwest Louisiana and southeast Texas during
the day Saturday.

...RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 9 AM TO 8 PM CDT
SATURDAY FOR HIGH WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR PORTIONS OF
CENTRAL AND SOUTHWEST LOUISIANA AND SOUTHEAST TEXAS...

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 027 Vernon, Fire Weather
Zone 028 Rapides, Fire Weather Zone 029 Avoyelles, Fire
Weather Zone 030 Beauregard, Fire Weather Zone 180 Tyler, Fire
Weather Zone 259 Northern Jasper and Fire Weather Zone 260
Northern Newton.

* TIMING...For the first Red Flag Warning, until 1 AM CDT
Saturday. For the second Red Flag Warning, from 9 AM to 8 PM
CDT Saturday.

* WINDS...North 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 30 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...Up to 72.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 16 at 5:51PM CDT until October 17 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
...STRONG NORTHERLY WINDS TODAY AND TONIGHT WILL INCREASE
WILDFIRE THREAT...

.A strong cold front will push south through Deep South Texas and
the Rio Grande Valley today, with a secondary surge of strong
northerly winds arriving late this evening through late Saturday
morning. Relative humidity values are expected to drop this
afternoon with little to no recovery into Saturday morning. Any
wildfire that can develop will behave dangerously with erratic
growth and spread due to strong winds and lower humidity. A Red
Flag Warning remains in effect.

* WINDS...North 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 45 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 24 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that can develop will behave dangerously
with erratic growth and spread.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 16 at 5:47PM CDT until October 18 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 13
feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 AM CDT Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

* WHERE...Apache Junction/Gold Canyon, Globe/Miami, Mazatzal

Carlos, and Superior.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM MST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Difficult driving conditions, especially for larger
vehicles traveling along roads with crosswinds. Light, unsecured
objects may become airborne. Localized channels of blowing dust may
briefly lower visibility under one mile.
properties.instruction:
A Wind Advisory means that sustained wind speeds of between 30 and 40
mph are expected, or wind gusts of between 40 and 58 mph. Winds this
strong can make driving difficult, especially for high profile
vehicles.

In addition, strong winds over desert areas could result in briefly
lowered visibilities to well under a mile at times in blowing dust or
blowing sand. Use extra caution.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 17 at 5:01AM ChST until October 18 at 4:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Guam, Rota, Saipan and Tinian.

* WHEN...Through Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains
and ditches may become clogged with debris. Extensive street
flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Tropical Storm Champi (29W) will drop copious amounts of rain
over Sunday and Monday...although an unexpected southward shift
in track will reduce these somewhat. Tinian and Saipan will see
around 4 to 6 inches, Rota could receive 10 to 15 inches, and
Guam might get 12 to 20 inches.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH SUNDAY AFTERNOON

properties.description:
...CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS POSSIBLE SATURDAY...

.A cold front will move through the area later today bringing
very dry air with RH values falling into the low to mid 30s along
with windy conditions with some gusts around 30 mph. The
combination of gusty winds, current drought conditions, ample dry
fuel, and very dry conditions will allow any fire that develops
to spread quickly.

The National Weather Service in New Orleans has issued a Red Flag
Warning all southern Mississippi and portions of southeast
Louisiana, which is in effect from 9 AM to 8 PM CDT Saturday. The
Fire Weather Watch is no longer in effect.

* AFFECTED AREA...Pointe Coupee, West Feliciana, East Feliciana,
St. Helena, Washington, Iberville, West Baton Rouge, East
Baton Rouge, Assumption, St. James, Wilkinson, Amite, Pike,
Northern Tangipahoa, Walthall, Southeast St. Tammany, Pearl
River, Northern St. Tammany, Southwestern St. Tammany,
Hancock, Central Tangipahoa, Harrison, Lower Tangipahoa,
Jackson, Northern Livingston, Southern Livingston, Western
Ascension and Eastern Ascension.

* WINDS...North 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 30 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.areaDesc: Aransas Islands; Kleberg Islands; Nueces Islands; Calhoun Islands
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 16 at 6:11AM CDT until October 18 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...Aransas Islands, Kleberg Islands, Nueces Islands and
Calhoun Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Saturday
evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 PM this
afternoon to 7 AM CDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the most experienced swimmers away from shore into deeper
water. These rip currents can become life-threatening to
anyone entering the surf.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
